handback.title: Settings may name only declared agent keys
handback.summary: A setting naming an agent key the shared workflow never receives is refused with one clear line.
handback.user_story: Owners who name an unusable agent key learn why in one line, from the audit and the run.

acceptance_criteria.text: Settings may name only the agent keys the entry workflow declares; a job refuses any other.
acceptance_criteria.words: The settings may name only agent keys `entry.yml` declares

edge_cases.case: A declared key other than Claude's still works.

acceptance_criteria.text: When settings name an undeclared key, the setup audit reports it in one line saying what to do.
acceptance_criteria.words: The setup audit reports, in one line, a setting that names any other key: it will never reach the jobs; use a declared name, or ask for that name to be declared in a release.

edge_cases.case: The undeclared key is set as a repo secret: still reported.
A declared key that is set gets no line.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a job's settings name an undeclared key, the job fails with the audit's line, not as missing.
acceptance_criteria.words: A job whose settings name an undeclared key fails with that same message, not as a missing key.

edge_cases.case: The undeclared secret is absent, as GitHub never passes it.

acceptance_criteria.text: The docs say settings may name only the declared agent keys, and any other never reaches jobs.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Docs are fixed text; no input varies.
